ov: Three species of very long, ribbon-shaped silver fish with a red crest and a dorsal fin running the whole length of the body. They live in the open ocean worldwide and are rarely seen alive. The giant oarfish is the longest bony fish, and a likely source of sea serpent stories.

why.et: Rarely caught; the larger species are fished on a small scale, but the flesh is gelatinous and not well regarded.

len: Giant oarfish usually about 3 m; record about 8 m
rg: Tropical, subtropical and warm temperate seas worldwide; the giant oarfish has been found from 72°N to 52°S.
df: Mainly zooplankton (krill, shrimp and other small crustaceans strained from the water), plus small fish, jellyfish and squid.
fx: It often sheds part of its own tail, and may do so more than once.
In Japan it is said to foretell earthquakes, but a 2019 study found the link to be an "illusory correlation".
